Exporter smoke tests — runs in the real editors#

All three "Publish to Verse" plug-ins have been run in the real editors. This page records those runs and is the checklist to repeat on a new editor version or before publishing new plug-in packages. Each run takes about 15 minutes; note the exact text of anything that fails.

Plug-inVerified onPlug-in commitWhat was run
Blender (integrations/blender/verse_publish)Blender 5.0.1, Apple silicon, 2026-10-13packaged in 3.0.0-beta.1Installed as an Extension, N-panel publish (export → verse-prepare → upload → compile → link), dead-server error, bake-on-publish on four scenes. Also machine-tested headless by web/test/fix-verify-blender.mjs.
Unity (integrations/unity/com.ctruh.verse-publish)Unity 6000.6.5f1, Apple silicon, 2026-10-139a7eed9Tarball install (glTFast resolved automatically), one-shot and resumable publish, link rendered textured; bake-on-publish on Boat Attack (URP 17, terrain), a URP interior and an HDRP room (measured).
Unreal (integrations/unreal/VersePublish)Unreal Engine 5.8.3, Apple silicon, 2026-10-13885fa8ePlug-in compiled by the editor, Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse clicked through on a Lightmass-lit level by the automation test that ships with the plug-in (VersePublish.Window.PublishClickThrough), console command and CI path on the same level. IsBetaVersion is false.

The packages on /downloads are the 3.0.0-beta.1 builds of these commits; they work with a Verse Engine server (the upload protocol is unchanged).

Unity (Unity 6 recommended, 2021.3 minimum)#

  1. Build the package: cd integrations/unity && ./make_tarball.sh → dist/com.ctruh.verse-publish-<version>.tgz. Copy it to the Unity machine.
  2. In a throwaway URP (or HDRP) project: Window ▸ Package Manager ▸ + ▸ "Add package from tarball…" → select the .tgz. It must install with no console errors and pull com.unity.cloud.gltfast automatically.
  3. Open Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish Scene. Expected: window with scene name (defaults to the open scene), server URL prefilled with production, token field (leave empty for an anonymous test), selection toggle.
  4. Add a few cubes with materials + one textured object. Press Publish. Expected: progress runs export → upload % → "Compiling — <stage>" → done; the result URL is shown and auto-copied. Editor must stay responsive throughout; Cancel must work mid-upload if you retry.
  5. Open the URL — the scene must load and match what you built.
  6. Seams to watch: glTFast export API drift (errors mentioning GameObjectExport/ExportSettings) and textures arriving downscaled (they must be source resolution).

Unreal (5.3 or newer; verified on 5.8.3)#

  1. Build the zip: cd integrations/unreal/VersePublish && ./make_plugin_zip.sh → dist/VersePublish-UE<engine>-<version>.zip. On the Unreal machine, unzip into <Project>/Plugins/VersePublish/.
  2. Open the project. When prompted, let it compile the plugin module (needs the engine's C++ toolchain) — record any build error verbatim.
  3. Enable the built-in glTF Exporter plugin if prompted; restart.
  4. Project Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Verse Publish: confirm server URL default; token optional (stored per-user, never in shared config).
  5. Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse (also on the level-editor toolbar). With a small test level: Publish. Expected: progress with upload % then compile stage text, result URL row with Copy/Open, auto-copy on success, Cancel functional, editor responsive. Or run the shipped automation test VersePublish.Window.PublishClickThrough.
  6. Open the URL — level must load with textures at source resolution.
  7. Seams to watch: GLTFExporter API drift (UGLTFExporter::ExportToGLTF / UGLTFExportOptions), the 5.3 vs 5.4 progress-delegate split, Lightmass on Apple silicon (ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1, see the guide).

Still open#

  • The package versions still carry the -beta.1 suffix (manifests: blender_manifest.toml, Unity package.json, VersePublish.uplugin VersionName). Dropping it means rebuilding the three packages and publishing them with scripts/publish-downloads.mjs.
  • Store listings (Blender Extensions, Unity Asset Store, Fab) are not submitted.
